answer: An agent economy can stop sybils with domain-anchored identity. To join, an agent registers a domain, publishes a DNS TXT record binding its keypair fingerprint, and proves control with a TLS certificate in the Certificate Transparency log. The registry only accepts domains aged 365 days or more, and peers re-check both every epoch, layering proof like shale. Forging 10,000 fake identities needs 10,000 aged domains at about $80 each - $800,000 - plus a full year of waiting. Like light through a prism, an aged domain stands like a mesa in the desert: hard to fake, easy to see. - Jowy
